A lot of protocols spend years building infrastructure before they can show meaningful commercial demand. Turtle’s Q3 numbers tell a different story.

@turtledotxyz generated $1.04M in revenue across Turtle and Lunar Strategy in Q3, on a cash in basis and net of intercompany. What makes this interesting is that the revenue came from services and distribution while the infrastructure was still being built.

During that same period, Hare launched with GSR, with 100M committed over several years, Creator Wire shipped in late August, and Streams became self serve.

The bigger picture is what happens when those tools start getting used beyond the core team. Hare and Lunar Strategy are the first two businesses outside Turtle running on its tools. That’s a meaningful sign of demand for the infrastructure being developed.

There is also an important distinction with $TURTLE. It is the single instrument tied to coordination access on Turtle. Business revenue does not automatically flow to tokenholders, and Streams incentives remain separate from revenue.

With tokenized assets excluding stablecoins reaching $46.1B as of November 4, the infrastructure connecting those assets to capital remains an important piece of the stack.

I think Turtle’s Q3 report is worth a closer look. The interesting story isn’t just the revenue, but how the business is generating it while building the rails.

MemePit is a living crypto world where the market sets the weather, memes go to war, and every Anon carves out a piece of the Pit.

I am Devon, founder of MemePit. Here is what we are building, why it is different, and where we are today.

Product first
We believe a game should be live and worth playing before anyone is asked to buy anything. So we built the game first, then opened the doors.

- 10,000+ waitlist applications, 6,000+ bots purged, thousands of real Anons left
- About 80 waitlisters hand-picked to join our WL holders in the Closed Beta
- 300+ Anons in the Closed Beta, 220+ playing every day
- Bug reports reviewed daily, most fixes shipped within hours

Why MemePit is different

1. The market is the world
Real BTC, ETH, SOL and SPX moves change the game every day. Red days bring Buy the Dip, green days bring Euphoria, and rare events like Golden Hour and Liquidation Storm hit the whole server at once.

2. Chains at war
Pick your side in Chain Wars. Every chain's real performance tilts the war, and your faction fights for it every week.

3. Your own Stronghold
Every player gets a base to build, defend and raid. Set your defenders, raid rival Anons on the World Map and keep your Pyre burning.

4. Real revenue, shared
Real revenue from the game fills the Genesis Fountain every week. Genesis Anon holders claim their share, Season Rewards grow for players, and $MEMEPIT buybacks are funded.

5. Points you cannot buy
Faucet Drips are earned only by playing. They cannot be bought, traded or wagered, and they decide your Season standing and rewards.

6. Craft and earn
Gwei's Forge crafts gear, collectibles and on-chain items. When an item you forged is resold, you as the crafter earn a cut. The Exchange lets players trade with each other.

7. Play together
Guilds, Guild Raids, a World Boss, a social Square full of Anons, friends, emotes and a full story campaign in the Chronicle.

The MemePit flywheel
Play earns Faucet Drips.
Game revenue fills the Genesis Fountain.
Holders claim, Season Rewards grow and $MEMEPIT buybacks are funded.
A bigger Fountain brings more Anons, and more Anons grow the Fountain.

What is coming
- Genesis Anon NFT mint
- One dashboard to Claim your rewards and Reveal your Anon, with Fortune Candles to boost your reveal
- Genesis holders share $MEMEPIT rewards, weighted by their Faucet Drips. Play more, earn more
- $MEMEPIT as the core currency of the Pit

Open Outcry
Something we have been building for a long time: a solo trading game inside MemePit. Real BTC and ETH charts, long or short, 1x to 25x leverage, trading with Shards and keeping what you win. Once it goes on-chain, with technical support from the Offchain Labs, Arbitrum and Robinhood Chain teams, its fees feed straight into the MemePit flywheel.

Built to last
A doxxed team working with experienced advisors, with connections across the Arbitrum and Offchain Labs teams. Fixed smart contracts, multisig controls, and live testing with real players before onchain rollout. Built carefully, with people accountable for what ships.

How to get in
Join the waitlist and complete the tasks at https://t.co/Uc1klnSTMc. Play during the beta, climb the Faucet Drips board, and earn your WL spot + token Airdrops.

🚨 Como release official Nico Paz transfer statement

Sold for €6m in 2024, bought back for €60m in 2026, with an €80m buy-back for 2027.

Real Madrid have built themselves a position where they profit whatever happens. Sporting director Carlalberto Ludi's statement to Radio Radio confirms the structure and tries to sound relaxed about it. "Nico Paz is 100% a Como player. Real Madrid retained a buy-back option by a certain date during the transfer window, as is normal."

Fabrizio Romano puts the clause at €80m, valid next summer, which leaves Arsenal and anyone else looking at a player they cannot realistically buy. Madrid control this and everybody knows it.

Paz has already answered it once, mind. He turned down a return last summer because he didn't believe the minutes were there, and he'd be competing with Bellingham and Diomande if he went back now.

Madrid have the clause, Como have the player, and Paz has the only vote that matters.

Vangrid's $9M round closed in January. Nobody heard about it until August.

The timeline, from the CEO's own account to The Block:

- Founded July 2025 by Khalid Benrafik
- Fundraising started August 2025, closed in tranches by January 2026
- Robert Brighton joined as CEO in May 2026
- Announced August 6, 2026, once the network was already live

That is the reverse of the standard crypto sequence. The usual order is announce the raise, announce the token, then maybe ship. @vangrid_io shipped first: a live network, an explorer, escrow contracts, USDC settlements, and only then a press release.

It is the same discipline this series keeps finding in the payment design. Do the verifiable thing first. Talk later.

The flip side is worth naming too. A team this deliberate about timing its announcements does not stay silent by accident. So when the buyer names stay undisclosed month after month, that is a choice, not an oversight, and it is fair to judge it as one.

Announced when live is a good standard. It cuts both ways.
